pr_body:
We did not report error if the password callback failed in the encrypted pkcs8 decoder.

Also the OSSL_DECODER_bio:unsupported was reported in cases where it just hid the real error. The fix for this is a little bit of hack so if you have a better idea how to fix this...

Fixes #14566
pr_comments: We kind of want a half-way error level between a fatal error and a failed to decode -- sort of a _I understand this and failed to decode because of X but if something else can handle it, use them_.  No doubt we'd then want quarter and three quarter error levels.....

issue_context.title: PKCS8 encoded RSA private key fail to decode if legacy algorithms are involved and the error reporting is lacking
issue_context.body:

const auto reason{ ::ERR_GET_REASON(::ERR_peek_last_error()) };

comments: Does the `openssl pkey -in encrypted-key.pem` work for you with this key?

The same issue there:
```
openssl pkey -in encrypted-key.pem
48280000:error:0680008E:lib(13):asn1_d2i_read_bio:reason(142)::0:
Could not read key from encrypted-key.pem
```

It does work with openssl 1.x. And it also works when using the decrypted private key file. Maybe the key is encrypted with a legacy cipher/hash which is excluded from the build, but then I would expect a different error code.
Ah, yes, it is - it is encrypted with single DES. You'll need the legacy provider loaded for that to be supported.
Certainly the error reporting is problematic, I agree with that.
The error reporting is a potential 3.0 blocker issue. But you'll still need to load the legacy provider to be actually able to load the key. That is not a real bug.
Related to #14423

#14834 has brought back error reports.  They aren't exactly the same, but are hopefully good enough.

Side note: when doing `openssl pkey -in foo.pem` with that key, I discovered a bug, where the passphrase is prompted for repeatedly. I'll make a separate commit for it.
Yep, I still see some rough edges with our error reporting.

The current master produces this when I use OSSL_DECODER to decode a PKCS8 RSA key with a bad password:
```

```

To summarize there is an error indicating possible bad password but it is behind the OSSL_DECODER_from_bio:unsupported error on the stack. @matbech Is it acceptable for you or not?

So apart from the unsupported error being the last on the stack, I think this is OK.
Hmmm, I thought I had coded it so that last "confusing" error report would only happen when there was no other error happening while decoding.

> So apart from the unsupported error being the last on the stack, I think this is OK.

I believe a more distinct error (than ERR_LIB_PKCS12 | PKCS12_R_PKCS12_CIPHERFINAL_ERROR) indicating a password mismatch should be in the error stack.

> I believe a more distinct error (than ERR_LIB_PKCS12 | PKCS12_R_PKCS12_CIPHERFINAL_ERROR) indicating a password mismatch should be in the error stack.

review_comments: Why are you removing this?  It's a perfectly legitimate report

Because it is not always an internal error. If you call OSSL_DECODER_from_bio() and not set the passphrase or passphrase callback in any way and try to decode encrypted key, this error will be raised. And the decoder will raise  `ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_PROV, PROV_R_UNABLE_TO_GET_PASSPHRASE);` anyway, if the callback fails.

I could raise a different error, but which one? Perhaps something like `ERR_raise(ERR_LIB_CRYPTO, CRYPTO_R_NO_PASSPHRASE_OR_CALLBACK)` ?

How about:

``` C
        ERR_raise_data(ERR_LIB_CRYPTO, ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT,
                       "No password method specified");
```
Thanks for the suggestion. Fixup pushed. @paulidale still OK?
